chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: Rock and roll drumming and studio work

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Right. Panama, speaking of him, was doing a lot of rock and roll dates in the '50s. Did you do any of those?
No.
That was his turf, huh?
Yeah. Yeah. I didn't do any rock 'n roll dates then. I like rock 'n roll drummer, it gives the drummer a free, he can do a lot of ad-libbing, and it's rhythmic.
Well at the time it was pretty close to R&B drumming, something like Lucky Millinder, shuffle.
Shuffle, the after beat.
Not like it is now.
Yeah, Panama had that sewed up, he was doing quite a bit of it.
Yeah, he was on a lot of hit records. You were on the Godfrey show then, right?
Yeah.
And we talked about that. Did you do anything else for CBS besides the Godfrey show? Around, that time?
No. That was it. Of course while I was on the Godfrey show, I did quite a few of those Jackie Gleason recording dates.
That Bobbie Packard was on.
Yeah, uh huh. Did quite a few of those.
And that was about it.
As far as studio work.

Yeah. I loved that studio work, though. It was good, you know. It's a wide range of things you're doing. Every day you didn't know what you were going to run into, you know, because we did a lot of Frank Sinatra dates. You didn't know what kind of arrangement you were going to play.
He did charts on the east, he did albums on the east coast?
Yeah. And what was his arranger's name that did a lot of charts for him?
Out on the West coast it was Nelson Riddle.
No on the east coast.
Axel Stordahl.
Axel Stordahl, that's the one, that's the one.
So that would be during the '40s then.
Yeah, that's right.
Before he went to the West coast.
That's right. Axel Stordahl.
Did you do much in the way of jingles and things like that?
A few, maybe with Raymond. Tony Mattola. That was about all, not too many.
